Note

Dissectability consists in the concretizations of a schematic particular being iteratively divisible into parts of the same kind: a mass of water can be divided into other masses of water; a chunk of wood can be further divided into other chunks of wood; a piece of gold can be divided into smaller pieces of gold; and so on. Despite the appearence of infinite divisibility, we know from chemistry that this dissectability is going to stop at either the molecular or the atomic level: for example, a water molecule has no smaller parts that are themselves water, and an atom of gold has no smaller parts that are themselves gold

loze is a top-level ontology after E. J. Lowe's four-category ontology, with Zemach's schematic particulars. Every term here is identified by an IRI under https://loze-ontology.org/.
